enjoyment_reasons: Authoring was pleasant: 80 lines of YAML, valid first time, good-looking slides in 0.3 s render plus 3 s thumbnails

findings.title: Installed skill teaches the raw-JSON/MCP workflow; the CLI's own get-started recommends a DeckSpec path the skill never mentions
findings.what_happened: SKILL.md opens with 'valid input for the generate_presentation MCP tool (or the CLI json2pptx generate -json)' and a recommend_visual -> show_pattern -> expand_pattern -> validate_input -> generate_presentation precondition chain. `json2pptx get-started` says the recommended path is a DeckSpec (list_slide_kinds -> validate_deck_spec -> render_deck_spec) and that the raw chain is a fallback. grep for DeckSpec / 'json2pptx semantic' / deck.yaml in the installed skill returns 0 hits. The skill also calls make_deck 'the recommended starting point when you don't need fine control' while get-started says 'make_deck is a skeleton/wireframe tool ... Never ship its output'. get-started points to 'SKILL.md -> QUALITY.md', which the installed skill does not contain. The skill carries no version stamp, so nothing told me it was behind (CLI reports skill_schema_version 4.159.0).
evidence: /Users/seb/.claude/skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md:13-14 and :227 (make_deck row)
log/getstarted.out: fast_path.tool=render_deck_spec; notes[1] 'Never ship its output'
ls generate-deck/: FINDINGS, PATTERNS, RULES, SKILL, TOOLS, WORKFLOW (no QUALITY.md); files dated May 22
log/plj.out vs skill text: 11 of 51 patterns unmentioned (next-steps, table-highlight, metric-list, text-sidebar, labeled-rows, ...)
findings.expected: The installed skill and the binary agree on the recommended workflow, or the binary tells me the skill is stale.
findings.suggestion: Stamp skill_schema_version in SKILL.md frontmatter and have `json2pptx skill-info` / `get-started` compare and warn; ship `json2pptx install-skill` (or `skill-info --check <dir>`) so the installed copy is refreshed with the binary.

findings.title: get-started on the CLI speaks only MCP tool names; a positional task is silently ignored
findings.what_happened: `json2pptx get-started` returns steps named list_slide_kinds, validate_deck_spec, render_deck_spec, render_deck_thumbnails, submit_visual_review with MCP args_template objects. Nothing says these are `semantic schema|validate|render` and `render-thumbnails` on the CLI. The mapping exists only as cli_counterpart inside the 90 KB `capabilities` output. Top-level help advertises 'get-started ... (brief|revise|validate-only)', but `get-started revise` answers task=brief with no warning; only --task works.
evidence: log/getstarted.out: 14641 bytes, no occurrence of a CLI command
log/cap.out: 90394 bytes; list_slide_kinds -> 'semantic schema', render_deck_spec -> 'semantic render'
`get-started revise` -> "task": "brief"; `get-started --task revise` -> "task": "revise"
semantic render blocking_reasons also name MCP tools: 'render_deck_thumbnails + submit_visual_review supply it'
findings.expected: When invoked from the CLI, each step carries the CLI command line to run.
findings.suggestion: Add a `cli` field per step (e.g. "json2pptx semantic validate --spec <file>"), accept the task positionally or reject unknown positionals, and add a 10-line 'CLI quick path' to top-level help.

findings.title: No CLI equivalent of list_slide_kinds: kind discovery is a 172 KB JSON Schema without examples
findings.what_happened: get-started promises 'compact kind summaries + copy-ready examples' from list_slide_kinds. Its CLI counterpart is `semantic schema`, which prints the whole draft 2020-12 schema (29 kinds, every alias duplicated in full) and has no examples. I wrote a Python filter to get a usable per-kind summary. Field descriptions point at MCP tools ('list_slide_kinds -> compositions[]', 'see get_chart_capabilities').
evidence: log/sem_schema.out: 172170 bytes; 'examples' present on 0 of 29 Slide_* defs
Slide_team repeats the 12-property member item schema three times (members, people, team)
findings.expected: A short listing of kinds with one-line purpose, required fields, limits and a copy-ready example, plus per-kind detail on request.
findings.suggestion: Add `json2pptx semantic kinds [--json]` and `json2pptx semantic kinds <kind>` (schema + example YAML), mirroring `patterns list` / `patterns show`.

findings.title: semantic render exits 1 while reporting ok:true, blocked by an info-level finding that cannot be waived
findings.what_happened: Every `semantic render` of the requested deck wrote a valid PPTX, printed {"ok": true, ...} on stdout, then printed 'Error: semantic render: deck written ... but not deterministically ready' and exited 1. The only deterministic blocker left was NO_EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY (severity info; describe-finding says severity review). The user fixed the 7 slides, so adding an executive summary was not an option, and `--strict off` did not change the exit code. The byte-identical file produced by `semantic compile` + `generate` exits 0 with success:true and score 100 (semantic render: 99). The exit codes are not documented in `semantic render -h`.
evidence: log/semrender3.out: "ok": true, "deterministic_ready": false; exit=1
log/semrender2_off.out: --strict off, exit=1, same blocking reason
sha256 6e8110fd351c... for both out/pitch.pptx (semantic render, exit 1) and raw/out/pitch_raw.pptx (generate, exit 0)
diagnostics: ('NO_EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY', 'info') vs blocking_reasons 'quality gate: deck storyline incomplete'
findings.expected: Exit 0 when the deck is written and no error-severity finding remains; one verdict for one artifact across both CLI paths.
findings.suggestion: Reserve non-zero exit for errors; report gate state in JSON (or a distinct documented exit code such as 2, as preflight does). Add `--gate off|warn|strict` or `--no-require-storyline`, and make the archetype (sales_pitch) decide whether an executive summary is required.

findings.title: render-thumbnails cannot write PNG files; images arrive only as base64 inside stdout JSON
findings.what_happened: The user asked for PNGs. `render-thumbnails` and `render-slide` have no output flag; they print png_base64 per slide (169 KB for 7 slides at 100 dpi, 276 KB at 150). Unredirected, that floods an agent's context. I had to write a Python decode step and choose file names myself. `inspect --images <dir>` expects slide-0.png, slide-1.png, ..., which no CLI command produces. The returned content_hash does not equal the SHA-256 of the PNG bytes delivered, although the skill says 'content_hash (SHA-256 of the PNG)'.
evidence: log/thumbs1.out: 168770 bytes, keys index/png_base64/content_hash/source_hash, no path
log/h_render-thumbnails.err: options are --density --force --max-slides --pptx --slides --templates-dir
slide 0: content_hash 67b5e5a4..., sha256(decoded png) 2d86b1b2...
preview-wireframe and export do have --out / --output-dir
findings.expected: `render-thumbnails --pptx deck.pptx --out-dir slides/` writes slide-01.png ... and prints a small manifest of paths.
findings.suggestion: Add --out-dir (and make file output the CLI default, base64 opt-in), name files the way `inspect --images` reads them, and either hash the delivered bytes or document what content_hash covers.

findings.title: Raw validate (without --fit-report) and generate both report success for a deck whose chart cannot render
findings.what_happened: Test deck with a typo'd key (contnt) and chart type stacked-bar. `validate --json` returned valid:true, exit 0, two warnings. `generate` returned exit 0 and success:true while its own report lists diagram_render_failed with severity error / action refuse and quality.issues '1 blocking finding(s)'; the PPTX contains a 'Data unavailable' placeholder and a blank first slide. Only `validate --fit-report` (exit 1), `preflight` (exit 2) and `generate --strict-fit=strict` (exit 1) refuse it. The --fit-report help text says only 'Run per-cell text overflow measurement'.
evidence: log/e_typo_validate.out: valid true, findings.ok true, '2 warnings'
log/e_typo_generate.out: success true; fit_findings [('diagram_render_failed','error','refuse'), ...]; quality.score 44
log/e_typo_pre.out: ok false, 'RENDER.diagram_render_failed', exit 2
findings.expected: A deck that will render a placeholder instead of its chart fails plain validate and makes generate exit non-zero by default.
findings.suggestion: Run the render-projection checks in default validate, make error/refuse findings fail generate unless --partial is set, and describe --fit-report accurately or fold it into the default.

findings.title: semantic validate passes a spec that semantic render then blocks; the stat text budget is not in the schema
findings.what_happened: `semantic validate` returned ok with one rhythm warning. Render then added BODY_TOO_LONG (stat label+context 129 chars against a combined ~120) and NO_EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY and blocked on both. The schema gives per-field limits (label <=80, context <=120), which my copy met; the combined limit only appears at render time. validate also takes no --template / --templates-dir, unlike compile and render.
evidence: log/semval1.out: ok true, '1 warning'
log/semrender1.out: BODY_TOO_LONG 'use 129 characters but the stack beneath the number holds about 120'
semantic validate -h: only --spec and --strict
findings.expected: validate reports everything render will block on.
findings.suggestion: Run the same gate in `semantic validate` (accept --template), and state the combined stat budget in the kind description.

findings.title: Input, output and slide-selection flags mean different things in different subcommands
findings.what_happened: Input file: positional for validate / read / validate-output / validate-template / patterns; `--json <file>` for generate / preflight / score / analyze-rhythm / preview; `--spec` for semantic; `--pptx` for render-* and export. On validate, `--json` is a boolean meaning 'emit JSON'. Output: `--output` (generate, file or dir; semantic render), `--output-dir` (export), `--out` (preview-wireframe), none (render-thumbnails). Slides: `--slide <n>` (preview-wireframe), `--slide <file>` (render-slide-from-json), `--slide-index` (render-slide), `--slides 1,3` (render-thumbnails). Flags after a positional are read as file names.
evidence: `score raw/pitch.json` -> usage + exit 1; `analyze-rhythm raw/pitch.json` -> 'Error: --json is required'
`validate raw/pitch.json --json` -> '--json: INVALID ... open --json: no such file or directory'
`render-thumbnails out/pitch.pptx` -> usage dump, exit 1
findings.expected: One convention: the input file positional everywhere (flag kept as alias), --format json for output shape, --out for outputs, --slide N for indices.
findings.suggestion: Accept the positional input on every command, rename validate's boolean to --format json only (keep --json with a deprecation note), and say 'flags must come before the file' when a flag-looking token is parsed as a path.

findings.title: Help goes to stderr and `-h` exits 1 on most subcommands
findings.what_happened: `json2pptx --help` writes 5.5 KB to stderr and nothing to stdout. Of 25 subcommands probed, 21 exit 1 on -h and end with 'Error: flag: help requested'; patterns, semantic (and its subcommands), icons and tables exit 0. `icons list -h` and `purge-render-cache -h` print Go's default single-dash style while the rest print double-dash. Default output differs too: patterns list, patterns validate, icons, tables, validate print human text; skill-info, score, preview, recommend-* print JSON.
evidence: log/help.out 0 B, log/help.err 5473 B, exit 0
generate -h: exit=1, last line 'Error: flag: help requested'; semantic validate -h: exit=0
icons list -h: 'Usage of icons list: -json ... -set string'
findings.expected: Help on stdout with exit 0 everywhere, one flag style, one default output format.
findings.suggestion: Handle flag.ErrHelp centrally (stdout, exit 0), and pick JSON-by-default with --human, or the reverse, across all subcommands.

findings.title: stderr carries repeated INFO logs and sometimes the only success signal or the error JSON
findings.what_happened: stdout JSON was never polluted, which is good. But one render logs each 'pattern expanded' line five times (30 lines for 6 patterns). A plain `generate` prints nothing on stdout; the output path is only in the stderr line 'INFO JSON conversion complete output=...'. `--json-output-report -` does print the report to stdout but that '-' is not in the help. Error envelopes go to stdout for `semantic validate` and `validate --json`, to stderr for `semantic render`, `render-thumbnails` and `describe-finding`; malformed JSON under `validate --json` yields plain text on stderr. Several CLI envelopes carry "subcommand":"mcp". With --strict-fit=strict the findings are printed twice (JSON on stdout, NDJSON on stderr).
evidence: log/semrender3.err: 30 INFO lines, each unique line x5
log/gen2.out 0 B; log/gen2.err 'INFO JSON conversion complete output=raw/out2/output.pptx'
log/e_sem_badtpl_render: stdout 0 B, JSON on stderr; log/e_thumbs_missing.err: "subcommand":"mcp"
log/e_malformed_validate_json.err: 'Error: invalid JSON in err/malformed.json: invalid character ...' (no line/column, not an envelope)
findings.expected: Result or error envelope always on stdout; logs quiet unless --verbose.
findings.suggestion: Default log level WARN (INFO under --verbose), dedupe the expansion log, print a one-line JSON result from generate, and send every envelope to stdout with the real subcommand name.

findings.title: validate --json has two response shapes and mixed slide index bases
findings.what_happened: On success the top level is {valid, slide_count, ..., findings:{ok, findings:[...]}}; on failure it is the bare envelope {ok:false, findings:[...]}. My one-liner that worked on the passing deck crashed on the failing one. Indices: where.slide and slides[4] are 0-based, quality.slide_scores[].slide_number is 1-based, and message text says 'slide 2' for /slides/1. The human summary reported 'Charts: 0' for a deck with a chart-insights-split chart.
evidence: log/val_j.out findings is a dict; log/e_typo_valfit.out findings is a list (TypeError in my parser)
log/val_h.out: 'Slides: 7 | Charts: 0 | Diagrams: 0 | Tables: 1 | Shapes: 1'
INPUT.takeaway_missing: message 'slide 2: ...' with evidence.path /slides/1
findings.expected: One shape with ok at a fixed location; one index base, or both given explicitly.
findings.suggestion: Always return the success shape with findings.ok false on failure, and add slide_index (0-based) and slide_number (1-based) to every finding.

findings.title: plan-deck drops most of an explicitly enumerated outline
findings.what_happened: Brief: '7-slide investor pitch deck ...: problem, solution, market size chart, traction KPIs, business model, team of 4, the ask' with --slides 7 --format deckspec. Result: 5 slides (title, executive_summary, stat, pillars, next_steps), deck title set to the brief text, no archetype, no chart/KPI/team slide. The raw format also returned 5. I discarded the plan and wrote the spec by hand. The default is --format raw although get-started recommends deckspec.
evidence: log/plan.out: budget_note 'The storyline needs 5 of the 7 slides'
log/plan_raw.out: 5 slides; slide 2 pairs team-bios with content_seed 'traction KPIs, business model'
findings.expected: A comma-separated outline in the brief becomes one slide per item with a fitting kind (chart_insight, kpi_snapshot, team, ...).
findings.suggestion: Parse enumerated outlines into slots before applying the storyline template, honour --slides when the brief lists that many topics, and set meta.archetype from words like 'pitch'.

findings.title: Slides scored 100 still show layout quirks: misaligned KPI value, blue highlight on a green template, half-empty slides
findings.what_happened: All slides were readable and shippable, but: on the KPI slide the card whose label wraps to two lines ('92%') sits higher than the other three; the table's highlight column and the corner triangle are blue (accent3 #1565C0) on forest-green; pillars, KPI and table slides fill roughly the top 40% and leave a blank band above the takeaway. None was reported. The one rhythm warning calls a table, team cards and a next-steps list '3 consecutive text slides'.
evidence: out/slides/slide-04.png (92% card), slide-05.png (blue highlight column), slide-02.png (empty band)
log/semrender3.out: slide_scores 100 for slides 3-7
log/explain1.out: visual_family 'text' for table, team, next_steps
findings.expected: Card values share a baseline; highlight uses the template's primary accent tint; sparse grids grow or centre vertically.
findings.suggestion: Align KPI values to a common baseline, tint highlight_column from accent1/lt2, vertically centre short grids, and give table / team / next-steps their own visual families.

findings.title: Undocumented sidecar file and large caches left behind
findings.what_happened: `semantic render` writes <name>.pptx.authoring.json (24 KB) next to the deck; it is named in the stdout manifest_path but not in -h, and there is no flag to suppress it. `generate --output <dir>` names the file output.pptx. On this machine $TMPDIR holds 2465 json2pptx-lo-* directories (617 MB) and a 27 MB render cache, and ~/.cache/json2pptx/layout-previews holds 28322 files (311 MB). These predate my session (dates back to Sep 19) and a forced render of mine added none, so I cannot attribute them to the CLI path. skill-info reports preview_cache_writes: true unless --no-preview is passed.
evidence: out/pitch.pptx.authoring.json 24400 B
`ls -d $TMPDIR/json2pptx-lo-* | wc -l` -> 2465; du total 617M
log/si_list.out side_effects: preview_cache_writes true
findings.expected: Only the requested artefact is written, or sidecars are opt-in and documented; temp dirs are removed on exit.
findings.suggestion: Document the sidecar in `semantic render -h` with --no-manifest, default the output name to the input basename, and have purge-render-cache also sweep stale json2pptx-lo-* dirs.
